what: Share of would-be leavers we keep after contact
why: Unknown (Vivian, round 2). Why 20%: about 4 in 5 reasons flagged customers give (price, rival, renewal) have a matching approved offer; we assume one in four of those would-be leavers accepts and stays. Below 2.6% the pilot loses money; 2.6%-6.2% makes money but cannot be proven in 90 days; 6.2%+ is proven.

what: Share of flagged customers who leave within 60 days without action
why: Measured on Mar/Apr/May 2026 cutoffs, notes before cutoff only.

what: Customers who take the offer per customer saved
why: Some customers who would have stayed also take the offer; this cost is counted.

value: monthly bill x months they keep paying (max 6)
why: Finance rule, confirmed by Vivian: six months of the full bill, stopping if they cancel. Flagged customers who are still with us after 60 days leave at about 12% a month (data), so a kept customer pays about 4.3 of the 6 months on average.

value: NT$2 per number dialled + NT$25 per conversation
why: Vivian: two charges, per conversation not per minute. Solved exactly from the 6 call campaigns in campaigns.csv; about 7.5% of dials became conversations. Care call-backs count toward the 2,000 a month.

what: Longer view, shown beside the 6-month credit
value: 24 months at the observed churn rate
why: Vivian: start with the six-month credit, a lifetime view may sit beside it. New customers: 1.8% monthly churn (postpaid average). Kept at-risk customers: their own higher rate.

what: Share of customers who asked about it in a note and then buy
why: Past broad upsell added about 0.16 points over holdout; asked-for offers should do better. Pilot measures it.
Audience uses notes from the last 90 days.
